01Project · Brand identity

Paul John. Matured in Goa.

A self-initiated identity concept for an Indian single malt: positioning, a three-voice type system, four label expressions, a Goan azulejos tile and a campaign, all from one idea: heat has a character.

Open the Figma file ↗
Idea

Brand idea

“Crafted in India. Matured in Goa.” The concept opens with a place-led promise and a bold, unapologetic wordmark: heat, craft, character, Goan heritage.

System

Positioning & visual vocabulary

Not borrowed heritage, an Indian original. A three-voice type system (Outfit for impact, Cormorant Garamond italic for poetry, IBM Plex Mono for facts) and a palette of cream, amber, copper, ink and terracotta, with an indigo drawn from Goa’s azulejos tiles.

Packaging

Four expressions, one voice

Nirvana, Brilliance, Edited and Bold share one label hierarchy: name, echo, character, tasting subtitles, origin. Each expression owns one colour and its own type voice, and an amber dot marks the peat position.

Pack & pattern

Goa, written in tile

Dark glass, a copper closure and a bottle band of indigo and cream, taken from Goan azulejos. The tile, with its compass roses and diamond motifs, carries through cartons, tissue wraps and tasting collateral.

Campaign

Three posters, one idea

“Goa turns up the heat.” “Born in Bengaluru. Matured in Goa.” “Tasting notes, subtitled.” Repeated type fades like heat in the air, and tasting notes are set as film subtitles, a nod to my background in kinetic type.

Open the Figma file ↗

An independent creative exploration, not official brand guidelines. Identity, packaging and campaign messaging are proposals, not approved brand assets, and packaging is illustrative. Bengaluru refers to John Distilleries’ company origin; the whisky is made in Goa. For adults of legal drinking age only.

02Project · Packaging & identity

Chatak. Thoda tangy. Poora fizz.

A concept brand for an Indian soft drink: street-stall flavours in a can, with a loud sans wordmark, a colour for every flavour and a folk-print pattern that ties the range together.

Open the Figma prototype ↗
Who it’s for16 to 30s who’d rather have jaljeera than cola.
The ideaChatak means that tangy zing. Every flavour is a street-stall classic with a face of its own.
The systemOne wordmark, one colour per flavour, a fruit illustration in a cream circle and the same three lines on every can.
Interactive

The full Chatak board as a Figma prototype. It opens in a new tab.

Figma prototype · Chatak brand worldScroll
the board.Open the prototype →
Brand world

Not subtle. Not sorry. A new-school soda with an old-school soul, built on nostalgia with the volume up.

Identity

A chunky wordmark, Bricolage Grotesque and Outfit, and one shared palette for four very different moods.

Packaging

Same gang, different tang. Colour-coded cans with fruit medallions make the family instantly recognisable.

Out in the wild

Hinglish headlines and a sticker-bomb language turn every touchpoint into a little celebration.

Digital extension

Same energy, smaller screens: a landing page concept and a social launch post.

A self-initiated concept, not a real brand.

05Academic projects

Design I made between lectures.

Self-initiated work from my film studies and psychology courses at JDSOLA. Same habits as the client work: one idea per piece, type doing the heavy lifting, and a layout built to be read.

Picture Abhi Baaki Hai · Podcast covers

Cover art for episodes of a podcast made in my Indian Cinema class at JDSOLA, where I was on the graphic design team. Collage and a single yellow type voice tie the series together, and the first cover layers Indic scripts for “traveller”.

Psychology assignments · Visual communication

Two assignments where I turned academic content into something people would actually want to read: a research poster on neuroaesthetics, and a magazine-cover take on adolescent development.

07About

Colour, type and a point of view.
